name: Luminaire general plan symbol
summary: General installation plan symbol for a luminaire or lighting point, drawn as a crossed circle at the ceiling position.
description: On IEC-style lighting plans a crossed circle marks the position of a luminaire or a lighting outlet. It is the base form that other luminaire symbols modify: lines are added for linear fittings, arrows for spotlights and letters for emergency or special types.

The symbol is placed to scale at the ceiling position and tagged with a fixture type letter keyed to the luminaire schedule. Switching lines connect it to switches, and circuit labels identify the lighting circuit.
The crossed circle on a plan is not a control panel indicator lamp, even though the graphic is similar. Context, scale and the schedule make the difference.
readingNotes: Read the fixture type tag against the luminaire schedule.
Follow switching lines to the switch positions.
drawingChecklist: Tag each luminaire with its schedule type.
distinction: The indicator lamp in control schematics uses a similar graphic but signals equipment state; the plan symbol locates a room luminaire.
